title: How Fast Can a Nerve Signal Travel?
description:
Some nerve signals can cross your body faster than a race car.

Fast myelinated nerve fibres can conduct signals at roughly 100–120 metres per second.

Speed depends on axon diameter and myelination; not all nerve signals travel this fast.

Myelin lets the electrical impulse jump between nodes in saltatory conduction.
